name: Colin McGinn
notes: Q3 yes: a natural brain property P produces experience, we just can't grasp it; Q13 no since qualia rest on hidden P.

name: Thomas Nagel
notes: Q1 unsure: hopes an expanded future science might, not current physics; Q13 no given protomental constituents.

name: David Eagleman
notes: Possibilianism drives Q5 yes; Q4 yes from his radio-receiver point in Incognito, while still leaning brain-based (Q3).

name: Sam Harris
notes: Q1 no: doubts the hard problem will be cracked; agnostic on whether brain suffices or consciousness is fundamental.

name: Michael Shermer
notes: Q1 no per his 'final mysterianism' column; otherwise standard materialist skeptic.

name: Michael Levin
notes: Q2 unsure: takes hard problem seriously but reframes it; Q6 drifting toward yes with his Platonic-space talk.

name: Paul Davies
notes: Q10 yes from fine-tuning/Goldilocks themes; Q11 no as he isn't a theist despite 'mind of God' language.

name: Raymond Tallis
notes: Q3 firm no (anti-neuromania) yet atheist and non-panpsychist, so Q6 and Q11 no.

name: George Musser
notes: Q4 no: thinks neuroscience and physics findings constrain theories; Q7 yes from sympathy to basal cognition and AI minds.

name: Robert Lawrence Kuhn
notes: Deliberately keeps options open, hence many unsure; Q12 no as a niche view he doesn't endorse.
